headline: GlobalFoundries has announced plans for FDX Fusion, a new chip-making platform for AI in robots, cars and other devices, to be produced in Dresden from 2028.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: an official roadmap with a production site and dates, but the performance goals are the company's own and production is two years away.
importance_line: It would add a European production line for chips aimed at robots, cars and factory equipment, which matters to carmakers, industrial firms and Europe's push for local chip supply, but the performance claims are targets and nothing is in production.
summary: GlobalFoundries said in a press release on 9 Oct 2026 that it plans to start making chips on FDX Fusion, a new version of its FD-SOI process (a chip-making method suited to low-power devices), in 2028 at its plant in Dresden, Germany; the first generation is expected to reach seven-nanometre-class digital performance with more than twice the density of its first-generation FDX technology. The company is aiming the platform at Physical AI (AI built into machines that sense and act, such as robots and vehicles), says it is working with several customers, and plans to give customers test silicon to evaluate in early 2027, with a first design kit in mid-2027.
notes: Official company press release read in full; it is a roadmap and every performance figure is the company's own expectation. Marketing wording ('world's most advanced') not used.
